title: revenue_ttm and net_income_ttm fabricate a TTM figure by synthesizing a phantom quarter for a company that has no true TTM
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JONJUA -> revenue_ttm: 239033504.0 (INR 23.9034 crore), net_income_ttm: 87482000.0 (INR 8.7482 crore), growth_basis: 'mrq_yoy'. Outside truth (screener.in, the only figure obtainable, since JONJUA has NO true trailing-twelve-months data -- it reported HALF-YEARLY until FY26 and only 3 discrete quarters have ever been filed: Dec-2025 sales 1.54cr/np 1.23cr, Mar-2026 sales 16.36cr/np 5.72cr, Jun-2026 sales 4.35cr/np 1.24cr) gives FY2025-26 full-year standalone revenue 21.21cr and net profit 8.07cr -- 12.7% and 8.4% BELOW the app's TTM figures respectively. Reconstructing the app's arithmetic: summing the 3 known filed quarters (1.54+16.36+4.35=22.25cr revenue, 1.23+5.72+1.24=8.19cr profit) plus HALF of the H1-FY26 half-year figure (FY26 total 21.21cr minus the two known H2 quarters 17.90cr = 3.31cr H1; half = 1.655cr revenue, and correspondingly ~0.56cr profit) reproduces the app's revenue_ttm (22.25+1.655=23.905, vs app's 23.9034) and net_income_ttm (8.19+0.56=8.75, vs app's 8.7482) almost exactly -- yfinance is treating half of a NEVER-FILED-AS-A-QUARTER half-year figure as if it were a discrete quarter to fill the fourth TTM slot.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P14_JONJUA.json:259-260,265 (revenue_ttm, net_income_ttm, growth_basis in the fundamentals body), :1029-1037 (income statement 'Total Revenue' 2026: 212051000.0 -- the real FY26 annual figure, 21.2051cr, differs from revenue_ttm), :769-807 ('Net Income Common Stockholders'/'Net Income Including Noncontrolling Interests' 2026: 82223000.0/80697000.0 -- both differ from net_income_ttm); sidecar/services/yfinance_provider.py:391-392 (revenue_ttm=_num(info.get('totalRevenue')), net_income_ttm=_num(info.get('netIncomeToCommon')) -- both taken verbatim from yfinance's own TTM computation with no app-side sanity check against the annual income statement fetched by the SAME service two routes over); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P14_JONJUA.json:509-517 (prior_quarters series), :626-628 (trap T6: 'There is NO true TTM for this company ... Any product that prints TTM for this name is asserting a number nobody has filed.')
notes: Principle violated: the pack explicitly names this exact failure mode as the highest-value trap in the collection, and the app falls into it precisely -- presenting a specific, decimal-precise 'TTM' revenue and profit figure for a company whose own reporting history makes a genuine TTM impossible to construct, built by silently averaging in a half-filed period as if it were a real quarter. Concrete consequence: a user comparing JONJUA's 'TTM' P/E, growth or profitability against peers is comparing against a number nobody at the company has ever filed or audited. Smallest fix shape: when a company's income-statement periods are annual-only or show reporting-cadence gaps (an explicit yfinance quarterly-financials call returning fewer than 4 well-formed quarters), suppress or clearly re-label the *_ttm fields as 'FY<year> annual' rather than presenting yfinance's own synthetic TTM as fact.

title: Equity Overview 'Insiders' shows 46.6% promoter/insider holding while the app's own shareholding-pattern endpoint correctly shows 29.7% for the same quarter
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JONJUA -> held_percent_insiders: 0.46623 (rendered as 'Insiders' in the Ownership section, src/modules/equity-overview/EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:141). GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/shareholding?symbol=JONJUA (same collection run) -> the Jun-2026 pattern (the app's own latest quarter) gives promoter_percent: 29.67 -- confirmed correct against screener.in's Jun-2026 shareholding table (promoter 29.67%, matches exactly, same as-of quarter). The two app fields disagree by 16.95 percentage points on the same fact for the same company at the same time.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P14_JONJUA.json:266 (held_percent_insiders: 0.46623), :2063 (disclosures/shareholding Jun-2026 pattern: promoter_percent: 29.67); src/modules/equity-overview/EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:141 (label 'Insiders', key held_percent_insiders); sidecar/services/yfinance_provider.py:398 (held_percent_insiders=_num(info.get('heldPercentInsiders')), no correction applied); sidecar/services/ownership_check.py:1-33 (the purpose-built NSE/BSE cross-check for exactly this yfinance failure mode is wired only into the research snapshot builder, per its own module docstring, never into the plain GET /fundamentals/<symbol> route the panel calls -- same wiring gap already identified for DHANBANK in DAT-P12-1, reproduced independently here on a different symbol with a different, larger error size).
notes: Principle violated: same root cause as DAT-P12-1 (a correction mechanism exists for exactly this yfinance failure class but is wired into only one of two consumers of the same raw fundamentals), reproduced on a second entity with a 17-point error -- confirming this is a systemic, not one-off, defect. Concrete consequence: any JONJUA viewer sees a materially wrong 'insider ownership' figure right next to a data path (the shareholding pattern) that already has the correct number for the same period. Smallest fix shape: route the plain /fundamentals/<symbol> response through the same ownership_check.get_exchange_ownership cross-check the research leg already has, preferring the exchange-sourced shareholding-pattern promoter_percent over yfinance's heldPercentInsiders whenever both are available for the same as-of quarter.

title: /disclosures/results hard-fails (502) for JONJUA because it always routes through NSE, even though the symbol is correctly resolved as BSE-only everywhere else
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/results?symbol=JONJUA -> HTTP 502, body {"detail": "nse_direct: 'JONJUA' is not a known NSE instrument"}. The same symbol resolves correctly to BSE:542446 via /resolve, /quotes, /fundamentals and /disclosures/shareholding in the same collection run, and BSE's own filing feed confirms Q1 FY2026-27 results were filed 2026-08-12 (sales 4.35 crore, net profit 1.24 crore, EPS 0.35).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P14_JONJUA.json:2432-2443 (results_calendar call: status 502, body.detail), contrast with :171-173 (resolve.resolved.exchange='BSE') and :2073 (shareholding pattern source='BSE') in the same file; sidecar/routers/disclosures.py:74-92 (get_results calls corporate_disclosures.get_results_calendar unconditionally, no exchange branch); sidecar/services/corporate_disclosures.py:335-340 (get_results_calendar calls nse_provider.get_results_calendar(bare) directly with NO BSE fallback -- contrast with the SAME module's get_shareholding, whose own docstring at :369-376 explicitly documents 'NSE-first, BSE-fallback with a MERGE for dual-listed names'); sidecar/services/nse_provider.py:359 (raises ProviderError(f"nse_direct: {symbol!r} is not a known NSE instrument") for any non-NSE symbol).
notes: Principle violated: this is a routing bug, not a missing-data gap -- get_shareholding already has the BSE-fallback pattern this needs, but get_results_calendar was never given it, so /disclosures/results 502s for every BSE-only listing (a meaningful share of the battery, i.e. every SME-only name). Previously filed once for DAL (DAT-P2-7); reproduced independently here with the exact code-level cause identified. Consequence: the entire quarterly-results/board-meeting-calendar surface is unusable for any BSE SME stock, including the just-filed Q1 FY27 numbers for this company. Smallest fix shape: give get_results_calendar the same NSE-first/BSE-fallback branch that get_shareholding already implements.

title: No structured corporate-actions (bonus/split/rights/related-party) surface exists anywhere in the app -- two 2026 bonus issues and a Rs 19.14 crore related-party deal are invisible except as unparsed PDF headlines
repro: grep -rln 'bonus\|corporate_action' sidecar/routers/*.py -> zero matches; no router or endpoint anywhere in the app returns a bonus/split/rights-issue/related-party-transaction ledger with ratio, record date and value. The only place any of this appears in the collected snapshot is /disclosures/announcements, which returns bare PDF-attachment headlines ('Board Meeting Outcome for Allotment Of Bonus Shares And Other Matters', 2026-09-07) with no parsed ratio, record date, share-count delta, or transaction value. Outside truth (BSE's CorporateAction API): TWO bonus issues hit this scrip in 2026 alone (5:40, record 2026-01-23; 7:24, record 2026-09-04, +7,955,966 shares, 29.2% dilution to existing holders' absolute count basis) plus a Rs 19,13,62,000 related-party acquisition of an intangible trade secret from the company's own Chairman-cum-MD -- 87% of the prior year's consolidated turnover and 1.7x the entire market cap, payable on demand and adjustable against new share issuance -- and a Fund Raising Committee formed with an unquantified pending dilution.
evidence: grep output over sidecar/routers/*.py (no bonus/corporate_action route); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P14_JONJUA.json:2364-2421 (announcements.body -- 3 of the 7 headlines reference the bonus/related-party sequence in prose only, category='Company Update'/'Board Meeting', no structured fields); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P14_JONJUA.json:410-483 (corporate_actions_2026, full entries with ratio/date/value/counterparty, sourced from https://api.bseindia.com/BseIndiaAPI/api/CorporateAction/w?scripcode=542446)
notes: Principle violated: for a product benchmarked against screener.in-grade coverage, corporate actions (bonus/split/rights/related-party) are core, not optional, and for THIS company they are the single most consequential story of 2026 -- a demanding user's share count, per-share ratios and governance risk assessment are all silently stale without this feed. Concrete consequence: a user holding JONJUA has no in-app way to learn their holding was diluted twice in nine months or that management just moved 1.7x market cap of company assets to themselves on credit. Smallest fix shape: add a /disclosures/corporate-actions route backed by the same BSE CorporateAction API already reachable for the manifest/collection tooling, surfacing type, ratio, record/ex/payment date and (for related-party items) counterparty and value.

title: ROE and ROCE are both blank/absent despite screener.in having clean, single-source values for both
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JONJUA -> roe: null (field_meta.roe.status='unavailable', reason='provider did not publish this field'); no 'roce' key exists anywhere in the response schema. Outside truth (screener.in Ratios table, single clean source, no cross-source disagreement): ROE 19.9% (Last Year), ROCE 19.64% (Mar-2026).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P14_JONJUA.json:251 (roe: null), :406-412 (field_meta.roe); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P14_JONJUA.json:206-220 (roe.value=19.9, roce.value=19.6, both sourced to screener.in with no disagreement recorded); sidecar/models/fundamentals.py (no roce field in the Fundamentals model at all)
notes: Same class of gap already filed for JUMBO (DAT-P7-4: 'ROE is blank and ROCE has no field at all'), reproduced independently here. Unlike DHANBANK (a bank, where ROCE is explicitly not a meaningful metric), ROCE is a normal and meaningful ratio for JONJUA and screener carries it cleanly. Smallest fix shape: same as DAT-P7-4 -- add a computed ROE fallback (net_income_ttm / stockholders_equity, labelled with basis) when the provider field is unavailable, and add ROCE as a modelled capability.

title: Sector/industry shown as 'Industrials / Specialty Business Services' where BSE and screener.in both independently agree on 'Services / Consulting Services'
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JONJUA -> sector: 'Industrials', industry: 'Specialty Business Services' (yfinance-sourced). Outside truth: BSE's own ComHeader endpoint (Sector='Services', IndustryNew='Services', Industry='Consulting Services') and screener.in's breadcrumb agree exactly with each other -- 'Services' / 'Consulting Services' -- while the app's yfinance-sourced label is a different top-level category from both.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P14_JONJUA.json:233-234 (sector: 'Industrials', industry: 'Specialty Business Services'); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P14_JONJUA.json:84-94 (identity.sector.value='Services', identity.industry.value references BSE IGroup 'Commercial Services & Supplies' / 'Consulting Services', both from https://api.bseindia.com/BseIndiaAPI/api/ComHeader/w?quotetype=EQ&scripcode=542446&seriesid=, corroborated by screener.in's breadcrumb per the pack's note)
notes: Same class of finding already filed for SAFE (DAT-P4-5, medium) and NAPEROL (DAT-P8-1, high). Consequence: any sector-based peer set, screen or comparison built on the app's label groups JONJUA with the wrong universe of companies entirely (note: the pack itself separately flags that BSE's OWN 'Services/Consulting Services' label is also misleading vs the real business -- that is a listing-exchange-classification problem, distinct from this finding, which is that the app disagrees with its OWN best-available outside sources, not just with reality). Smallest fix shape: where the app already has a BSE-sourced sector/industry string (via the /resolve or /disclosures paths) prefer it over yfinance's frequently-miscategorized sector taxonomy for Indian small-caps, or surface both with clear provenance labelling.

title: A confirmed, sourced, nonzero trailing-12m dividend (Rs 0.10/share, paid 27-Oct-2025) renders as a blank TTM field, and no dividend event date (record/ex/payment) is surfaced anywhere
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/JONJUA -> dividend_per_share_ttm: null; no record_date/ex_date/payment_date field exists anywhere in the fundamentals response or the dividend-related schema. Outside truth: the company's only-ever dividend (Rs 0.10/share final dividend) was declared 2025-09-03, record date 2025-09-20, and PAID 2025-10-27 -- squarely inside the trailing 12 months from the 19-Sep-2026 collection date, and BSE's CorporateAction feed carries all three dates.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P14_JONJUA.json:268 (dividend_per_share_ttm: null); docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P14_JONJUA.json:288-319 (dividend.last_declared_per_share.value=0.10, record_date=2025-09-20, ex_date=2025-09-19, payment_date=2025-10-27, paid_trailing_12m_per_share.value=0.10, all sourced to https://api.bseindia.com/BseIndiaAPI/api/CorporateAction/w?scripcode=542446)
notes: Unlike the confirmed-ZERO cases already filed across the battery (DAT-P2-8, DAT-P3-3, DAT-P6-7/8, DAT-P7-5, DAT-P10-4, DAT-P11-2, DAT-P12-3 -- all 'blank instead of a known zero'), this is a confirmed NONZERO dividend that a user actually received rendering identically to 'never fetched'; the record/ex/payment-date gap mirrors DAT-P9-3 (no dividend-date field or endpoint anywhere in the app). Smallest fix shape: derive dividend_per_share_ttm from the same BSE CorporateAction dividend history the pack itself used (or the trailing-12m derivation already scoped for other DAT-P12-3-class findings), and add record/ex/payment date fields to the dividend surface.
